SHORTLIST METHOD

Use a simple 4-step broker check

  1. Choose the account first. Decide whether you need an ISA, GIA, SIPP or a Nigeria-facing account.
  2. Match the market. Make sure the platform actually offers the assets and exchanges you want.
  3. Price the full journey. Include platform fees, dealing, FX, transfers and withdrawal costs.
  4. Verify before funding. Use the official website and regulator register; never send investment money to a person or private account.
IMPORTANT

A cheaper broker is not automatically the better broker.

Service, investment range, tax wrappers, currency costs, support, transfer rules and your own experience level all matter. Investments can fall in value and you may get back less than you invest.

WHAT YOU MAY NEED

Before you start

  • Your legal name and personal contact details
  • Identity and address information for verification
  • Tax and source-of-funds details when requested
  • A personal bank account held in your own name
BEFORE YOUR FIRST ORDER

Check these carefully

  • Which market you are using and whether the security is available
  • The trading currency and any exchange-rate impact
  • Platform fees, funding method and withdrawal rules
  • The exact company, ticker, exchange and key risks
IMPORTANT RULE

Never rush the setup

Do not act on chat messages, private account details, or “guaranteed allocation” claims. Use official sources only and keep a record of confirmations, deposits and order details.

DIY MONTHLY INVESTMENT PLAN

Build a contribution habit you can actually repeat

Start with an amount you choose, build a simple structure you understand, and repeat it without CEO Hub handling your money or placing trades. The examples below are educational templates—not recommendations or promises of return.

THE GOALRepeatability

A good monthly plan is one you can afford through normal months—not one that depends on perfect markets.

1

Protect bills and emergency savings

2

Choose the amount yourself

3

Review, record and repeat

THREE EXAMPLE STARTING LEVELS

Choose a template, then make it yours

The figures are contribution examples only. You decide whether to use them, reduce them, increase them, or use a completely different amount.

STARTERKEEP IT SIMPLE

Build the habit

£100/mo

£1,200 contributed over 12 months

Possible structure to explore

One diversified core category; optionally keep the plan this simple while learning.

Your monthly job

Choose one contribution date, preview fees, make the contribution yourself, record it.

  • Suggested review rhythm: every 6 months
  • Suggested rule: do not add complexity just because markets are exciting
  • Suggested upgrade trigger: increase only when your budget comfortably allows it
BUILDERCORE + STABILISER

Build the base

£500/mo

£6,000 contributed over 12 months

Possible structure to explore

For example, 70–90% core and 10–30% stabiliser; you choose the actual mix.

Your monthly job

Use one or two planned purchases, avoid impulse additions, and record the reason for each.

  • Suggested review rhythm: quarterly
  • Suggested rule: keep any new category small until you understand it
  • Suggested checkpoint: compare total fees and FX costs every quarter
GROWTHMORE STRUCTURE

Broaden carefully

£1,000/mo

£12,000 contributed over 12 months

Possible structure to explore

For example, 60–80% core, 10–30% stabiliser and 0–20% optional satellite.

Your monthly job

Follow a written allocation, preview every order, and resist changing the plan because of headlines.

  • Suggested review rhythm: quick monthly check + quarterly review
  • Suggested rule: satellite ideas remain optional—not compulsory
  • Suggested control: keep a written reason for every allocation change
YOUR FIRST 3 MONTHS

Do it yourself, one month at a time

This sequence is designed to make the habit manageable rather than constantly changing investments.

MONTH 1

Set the foundation

  1. Check bills, debts and emergency savings.
  2. Choose your monthly amount.
  3. Choose and verify the account/provider route yourself.
  4. Write a simple allocation you understand.
  5. Preview costs before making the first contribution.
  6. Save the confirmation and one sentence explaining what you did.
MONTH 2

Repeat—do not reinvent

  1. Confirm the amount still fits this month.
  2. Check whether your chosen allocation is still the plan.
  3. Make only the planned contribution.
  4. Record fees, FX and confirmation.
  5. Note any questions instead of making impulsive changes.
MONTH 3

Review the system

  1. Total what you contributed—not what you hoped to earn.
  2. Check whether the routine felt affordable.
  3. Review fees and account friction.
  4. Ask whether your allocation is still understandable.
  5. Keep, simplify or adjust the process for the next quarter.
STEP-BY-STEP REPEATABLE METHOD

The 7-step monthly success method

“Winning” here means following a controlled process—not guaranteeing a profit. The member makes every decision and every transaction themselves.

METHOD PROGRESS0/7
1
PROTECT

Protect the foundation first

Check bills, essential spending, expensive debt and emergency savings before deciding this month’s contribution.

2
LIMIT

Set the amount before looking at markets

Choose the maximum amount you can comfortably contribute this month. Do not increase it because a market move looks exciting.

3
VERIFY

Verify the account and provider

Confirm the account route, provider, regulation, currency, fees and funding method using official information.

4
CHOOSE

Choose from your written plan

Use the allocation you already understand. Research anything new first and put impulse ideas on a watchlist instead of buying immediately.

5
PREVIEW

Preview the order before submitting

Recheck the investment, ticker or fund, amount, currency, fees, order details and the worst-case loss you are prepared to accept.

6
RECORD

Record what you actually did

Save the confirmation and note the amount, fees and one sentence explaining why the contribution matched your plan.

7
REVIEW

Review the process—not every market move

At the scheduled review, check affordability, fees, allocation drift and whether the plan is still understandable. Keep, simplify or adjust deliberately.

✓ A “good month”

You followed your written process, stayed within budget and recorded the decision—even if markets later fell.

✕ A “bad method”

Chasing headlines, increasing the budget impulsively, borrowing to invest, or buying something you cannot explain.

↻ The edge

Consistency, cost awareness, diversification, patience and scheduled review can improve decision quality; none can guarantee returns.

INVESTMENT TYPES AND RISK

Understand the possible loss first

Risk is not only price movement. Also check liquidity, inflation, credit, currency, concentration and fraud risk.

TypeTypical risk levelMain risksLiquidityPossible roleResearch
Cash savingsLowerInflation and provider risk above protection limitsHigh to mediumEmergency reserve and short goals
Government bondsLower to mediumInterest-rate, inflation and issuer riskUsually medium/highIncome and diversification
Diversified funds/ETFsMediumMarket, currency, tracking and concentration riskUsually highLong-term diversified core
Individual sharesMedium/highCompany, valuation and concentration riskVariesOptional researched allocation
Property/REITsMedium/highRates, vacancy, leverage and property-cycle riskLow for property; higher for REITsIncome and real assets
Private/speculativeVery highTotal loss, illiquidity, dilution and fraudLow/uncertainOnly money affordable to lose
High risk means real loss: diversification and regulation do not guarantee returns or prevent market losses.

PROP FIRM EDUCATION · RESEARCH FIRST

12 Prop Firms to Compare Before You Pay

Compare evaluation style, asset class, rules, payout structure and the real trade-offs before buying a challenge. These are research options—not endorsements, and programme terms can change.

YOUR RULE Rules before rewards.

A prop-firm evaluation can be simulated. Passing a challenge does not automatically mean you are trading a live brokerage account.

01
Structured risk limitsDaily/max loss rules can force discipline—but breaching them can end the account.
02
Lower capital at riskYou normally risk the evaluation/activation fees rather than depositing the advertised account size.
03
Performance rewardsSuccessful traders may earn a share of simulated trading profits subject to each firm’s rules.
04
Possible scaling pathSome firms offer larger simulated accounts or a route toward live capital after consistent performance.
POTENTIAL ADVANTAGES

Why traders consider prop firms

  • Access to a larger simulated account without personally depositing that headline balance.
  • Clear profit, drawdown and consistency rules can create a disciplined framework.
  • Some programmes include scaling, performance rewards and a possible path to live capital.
  • Useful for testing whether a strategy can survive strict risk controls.
REAL DISADVANTAGES

What can go wrong

  • Challenge, reset or activation fees can be lost when rules are breached.
  • Drawdown, consistency, news, overnight and payout rules may be stricter than your normal strategy.
  • Many “funded” stages remain simulated rather than a personal live brokerage account.
  • Terms, platforms, eligibility and payout rules can change, so old reviews may be misleading.
1-StepOne evaluation phase. Faster route, but usually tighter discipline is still required.
2-StepTwo performance phases. Often more gradual, but takes longer to complete.
Instant / ZeroSkip or reduce evaluation stages. Usually compare higher cost and stricter funded-stage rules.
FuturesContract limits, trailing/EOD drawdown, trading hours and data/platform costs matter most.

BEFORE YOU BUY ANY CHALLENGE

The 7-step prop-firm verification method

Do this yourself before paying. The firm’s maximum loss limit should be your emergency boundary—not your normal daily risk budget.

1Choose the asset class

Decide first: CFD/FX-style programme or exchange-traded futures. Do not choose from advertising alone.

2Open the official rulebook

Write down the profit target, daily loss, total drawdown, consistency, minimum days and time limit.

3Calculate the full cost

Add evaluation fee, resets, recurring billing, activation, data/platform fees and withdrawal charges.

4Check strategy restrictions

Verify news trading, overnight/weekend holding, EAs, copy trading, scalping and prohibited conduct.

5Read payout conditions

Check buffer, minimum profitable days, payout frequency, split, consistency and KYC requirements.

6Practise the exact rules

Use demo/paper trading first. If your strategy repeatedly breaches the rules, the challenge is not yet suitable.

7Start with the smallest sensible test

Never use rent, bills, emergency savings or borrowed money for challenge fees.

PROP FIRM RELEASE GATE

Complete the eight controls

Tick these only after you have checked the current official terms for the exact programme you want.

Verification: a prop-firm account may be simulated and is not the same as a personal brokerage account. Check the legal entity, current rules, payout terms, jurisdiction eligibility and complaints directly. Programme features can change without notice.
